title: Argentine Confederation
capsule: The Argentine Confederation was the loose federal union of Argentine provinces that emerged from the 1831 Federal Pact, with Juan Manuel de Rosas of Buenos Aires dominating as governor and de facto strongman until his defeat at the Battle of Caseros in 1852. Following Rosas's fall, Justo José de Urquiza convened the Santa Fe constitutional convention, which produced the Constitution of 1853 establishing a formal confederation with its capital at Paraná — distinct from the rebellious Buenos Aires province, which remained separate until 1861. The city of Buenos Aires rejoined after defeating Urquiza at the Battle of Pavón in September 1861, after which Bartolomé Mitre assumed the presidency and the unified Argentine Republic gradually superseded the confederation structure.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is moderately attested; provincial boundaries are documented in the 1853 constitution and contemporary maps, but effective control over frontier regions (Patagonia, Chaco) was nominal during this period, introducing some uncertainty at the edges.
